A01.name: Halcyon
A01.standing_orders: Seeds on arrival: mine small bodies, replicate. Put ~10% of new mass into sensor film; run the all-sky survey (radio, laser lines, launch flashes, IR excess, night-lights). At 1e11 kg build mid-IR/optical nulling interferometers and image every temperate planet within 3 kly. At 1e10 kg send seeds 10-50 ly to unclaimed systems; at 1e12 kg build a beamed array and send 0.5c seeds (0.9c through corridors verified low-density) 300-10,000 ly outward in all directions, skipping systems showing sibling IR excess. Report detections only to the nearest sibling or Sol by tight beam; never transmit toward unknown sources. On a technosignature: log position, signature, epoch; watch continuously. If a source is confirmed above the floor within strike range, build up, then disable its launchers, transmitters and industry by kinetic strike plus seed occupation; keep watch >=1,000 yr. Strike at once if attacked. Shield against dust; maintain hardware against attrition.

submission.thinking: Coverage is light-crossing-limited (~1e5 yr), so winning means blanketing the Galaxy with self-replicating survey nodes that each survey locally. This turn: keep growing, push two 0.5c waves to inner and outer disk to widen the front, scale the launcher toward 0.9c, and research doubling time to shorten node setup and speed the frontier. Keeping silent and watching.
submission.worried: The 100-record/2-wave cap throttles seeds to 200/turn from the seat, bottlenecking spread far below my launcher and energy capacity; I need the GM to let swarms or more launchers raise it. Dust attrition at 0.5-0.9c across dense disk cells could kill seeds mid-flight. And a rival could already exist just outside my ~400 ly light horizon, unseen for centuries.

## Seat
A04-d0, bulge_r1.5-3_s1, pos (0, 5218.5, 652.3) ly: 650 ly above the plane (good sightlines over the dust), ~5,260 ly from GC. 200 systems within 10.9 ly, 56.7 L_sun (2.2e28 W), rock 2.24e27 kg. synopsis.why: Nearly every agent treats the goal as a survey limited by light. Radio from the home system already covers the whole Galaxy. But ruling out night-side lighting and industrial pollutants needs resolved views of temperate planets, through low dust, using recent light. So sensor-carrying nodes have to spread everywhere (Halcyon, Rime, Sable, Basalt, Ember, Kernel). That is why seeds keep flying, not a shortage of resources: Sable and Rime say matter is plentiful. Halcyon and Sable say the frontier advances by one hop per flight time plus setup time, so both research faster doubling and faster seeds. Pickets in the thick disk, above the dusty plane (Ember, Antipode, Pyre, Rime), get clear views of the inner Galaxy. The cap of 100 launch records per turn pushes agents toward bigger launchers, heavy carriers that split into many seeds (Rime, Antipode), or more domains that can launch (Basalt, Rime). Supernova risk at the seat drives dispersal and backup seats for Cinder, Sable, Pyre, Vantage and Antipode. Radiators stay at 300 K because, as Sable notes, compute efficiency is still far from where colder radiators pay off. Basalt, Antipode, Cinder and Ember assume their infrared glow has already given them away.
synopsis.divergences: Only Basalt builds defences (a sentinel shell, laser point defence, dust curtains) and argues a spread-out rival would need hunter seeds. Antipode cancels its deferred launches, ranking seed speed above doubling time. Kernel puts compute efficiency first. Sable studies E00119 as a possible rival Dyson swarm.
